note: Two cases about repaying loans. In the first, a lender told a borrower to repay him in front of two named men, but the borrower repaid in front of two others. Abaye said two witnesses are two witnesses; Rava answered that naming them was meant to rule out exactly that. In the second, a lender asked to be repaid in front of two men learned in law, but the borrower paid him privately, and the money was later lost through no fault of the lender. The lender told Rav Nahman he had held it only for safekeeping until the condition was met. Rav Nahman ruled it a proper repayment: he and Rav Sheshet were learned men, so if the lender insisted on the condition, let him bring the money and be repaid before them.
why: Rava has just ruled on when a loan must be repaid in front of witnesses, and the Gemara now lists a series of real cases about loans, witnesses and repayment.

terms.meaning: Property held for someone else. A person holding it for free is not liable if it is lost through events beyond his control.
